subject: general
question: When a Tirthankara leaves a mortal body, it is known as ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nirvana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nirvana:**

 
 
• In Jainism, when a Tirthankara, a spiritual teacher who has conquered the cycle of birth and death (samsara) and shown the path to liberation, leaves their mortal body, it is known as Nirvana or Moksha.
 
• This signifies the complete liberation of the soul from all karmic bondage and its attainment of a state of eternal bliss and freedom.
 
• Nirvana is the ultimate goal of Jainism.
 
• It is achieved through the elimination of all karmas, which are accumulated through actions, thoughts, and words.
 
• A Tirthankara, having achieved Kevala Jnana (omniscience), preaches the path to liberation.
 
• Upon reaching the end of their lifespan, they relinquish their physical body, achieving Nirvana.
 
• This is not considered death in the conventional sense, but rather a final release from the cycle of rebirth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tapa Kalyana:**

 
 
• Tapa Kalyana refers to the auspicious event of a Tirthankara's renunciation of worldly life and the adoption of asceticism.
 
• This is a significant step on the path to becoming a Tirthankara.
 
• It's not related to the Tirthankara leaving their mortal body.
 
 
 
• **Siddhashila:**
 
 
• Siddhashila is the abode of the Siddhas, the liberated souls who have achieved Nirvana.
 
• It is considered to be beyond the three realms of existence (lower world, middle world, and upper world) and is the ultimate destination for those who have broken free from the cycle of birth and death.
 
• It's the place where the soul resides after achieving Nirvana, not the event of leaving the body.
 
 
 
• **Janma Kalyana:**
 
 
• Janma Kalyana refers to the auspicious birth of a Tirthankara.
 
• This is one of the five major auspicious events (Panch Kalyanakas) in a Tirthankara's life.
 
• It is a joyous occasion celebrated by Jains.
 
• It precedes the Tirthankara's renunciation and eventual attainment of Nirvana.
